Compute Bioclimatic and Thermal Stress Indicators

Source: R/sus_climate_compute_indicators.R
sus_climate_compute_indicators.Rd

sus_climate_compute_indicators() calculates a comprehensive set of bioclimatic and thermal-stress indices from INMET station data (output of sus_climate_inmet() or sus_climate_fill_inmet()).

Use it after sus_climate_inmet() / sus_climate_fill_inmet() and before sus_climate_aggregate(), sus_climate_compute_heatwaves() or sus_climate_compute_coldwaves() (which use wbgt_c, utci_c, hi_c). The output keeps the temporal resolution of the input (hourly for INMET) and contains only the identifier columns and the computed indicators (plus station metadata), unless keep_source_vars = TRUE. Indicators whose input columns are missing are returned as NA with a warning.

Scientific robustness highlights:

  • WBGT uses a dual wet-bulb estimate (Liljegren + Bernard/Pourmoghani) averaged for numerical robustness; solar radiation NA treated as 0 (no solar load at night) so all hours yield a valid value.

  • HI implements full Rothfusz (1990) regression with both NWS humidity adjustments and a regionally adapted validity threshold.

  • UTCI uses a Fiala-polynomial-inspired multi-term regression (vapour pressure, logarithmic wind, radiation linear + non-linear, wind vs radiation interaction).

  • PET is based on a MEMI-style energy-balance approximation with seasonal clothing adjustment and regional correction.

  • Solar radiation undergoes optional physical consistency verification against extraterrestrial radiation limits.

  • Diurnal range is a true daily aggregate (Tmax - Tmin per calendar day) broadcast to all hourly rows of that day.

  • Multi-level confidence flags (_flag_extreme, _flag_high, _flag_low) replace a single _out_of_range flag.

  • Optional 200-simulation Monte Carlo uncertainty estimation.

Available indicators:

CodeOutput columnRequires
wbgtwbgt_cT, RH, SR, WS
hihi_cT, RH
thithi_cT, RH
wcetwcet_cT, WS
wctwct_cT, WS
etet_cT, RH, WS
utciutci_cT, RH, WS, SR
petpet_cT, RH, WS, SR
cddcdd_cT
hddhdd_cT
gddgdd_cT
diurnal_rangediurnal_range_cT (daily agg.)
vapor_pressurevapor_pressure_kpaT, RH
heat_stress_riskheat_stress_riskT, RH, WS, SR
koppen_humiditykoppen_humidityRH

(Where: T=tair_dry_bulb_c, RH=rh_mean_porc, SR=sr_kj_m2, WS=ws_2_m_s)

Usage

sus_climate_compute_indicators(
  df,
  indicators = "all",
  region = "auto",
  datetime_col = NULL,
  station_col = NULL,
  apply_validity_mask = TRUE,
  confidence_flags = NULL,
  custom_thresholds = NULL,
  keep_source_vars = FALSE,
  verify_physics = TRUE,
  compute_uncertainty = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  lang = "pt",
  use_cache = TRUE,
  cache_dir = "~/.climasus4r_cache/spatial"
)

Arguments

df

A climasus_df at stage "climate" or later, typically from sus_climate_inmet() or sus_climate_fill_inmet() (a plain tibble or a lower-stage object errors). Needs a datetime column, a station column (station_code) and the input columns listed in the table above.

indicators

Character vector of indicator codes (case-insensitive), e.g. "wbgt" or c("wbgt", "hi", "utci"), or "all" (default) for the 15 codes in the table. Unknown codes error and list the valid ones.

region

Single character string selecting regional thresholds and parameters. "auto" (default) detects the biome from the UF column (most frequent UF) or, failing that, from mean latitude. Otherwise one of "amazon", "cerrado", "caatinga", "atlantic_forest", "pampa", "pantanal", "southeast", "south". "none" disables regional adaptation (standard thresholds, no confidence flags by default). An unknown value gives a warning and falls back to "southeast".

datetime_col

Single character string or NULL (default, auto-detected): name of the datetime column.

station_col

Single character string or NULL (default, auto-detected): name of the station identifier column.

apply_validity_mask

Logical scalar (default TRUE). Only effective when region = "none": masks HI, WCET and WCT outside their valid meteorological domains with NA.

confidence_flags

Logical scalar or NULL (default). Add <indicator>_flag_extreme, _flag_high, _flag_low columns. NULL means TRUE when a region is used (any region except "none", including "auto") and FALSE for region = "none".

custom_thresholds

Named list overriding the regional parameter values (merged with utils::modifyList()), or NULL (default). Names must match the entries of the regional parameter table. Ignored for region = "none".

keep_source_vars

Logical scalar (default FALSE). If TRUE, also returns the input columns required by the requested indicators.

verify_physics

Logical scalar (default TRUE). Check solar radiation against extraterrestrial limits; requires a latitude column and sr_kj_m2.

compute_uncertainty

Logical scalar (default FALSE). Adds <indicator>_ci_low / _ci_high columns (Monte Carlo, 200 simulations, 95% interval) for indicators that define input uncertainties.

verbose

Logical scalar (default TRUE).

lang

Single character string: "pt" (default), "en", "es".

use_cache

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), the station metadata table (downloaded once from the climasus4r GitHub repository, so a network connection is needed the first time) is read from and saved to cache_dir. If FALSE it is downloaded every call.

cache_dir

Single character string, directory for the cached station metadata. Default "~/.climasus4r_cache/spatial".

Value

A climasus_df with one row per input row containing date, the station column, one column per computed indicator (names in the table above, NA when skipped), optional flag/CI columns, optional source variables and the station metadata columns joined by station_code. sus_meta(): stage = "climate", type = "indicators", system = NULL, with the requested indicators in temporal$indicators_requested.

Scientific References

  • Liljegren et al. (2008) J. Occup. Environ. Hyg. 5(10):645-655.

  • Bernard & Pourmoghani (1999) AIHAJ 60(1):32-37.

  • Rothfusz (1990) NWS Tech. Attachment SR/SSD 90-23.

  • Thom (1959) Weatherwise 12(2):57-59.

  • Environment Canada (2001) Wind Chill Index.

  • Brode et al. (2012) Int. J. Biometeorol. 56(4):481-494.

  • Matzarakis et al. (1999) Int. J. Biometeorol. 43:76-84.

  • Magnus (1844) / Tetens (1930) saturation vapour pressure.

See also

sus_climate_inmet(), sus_climate_fill_inmet(), sus_climate_aggregate(), sus_climate_compute_heatwaves(), sus_climate_compute_coldwaves()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
result <- sus_climate_compute_indicators(df_clima)

result <- sus_climate_compute_indicators(
  df_clima, region = "amazon", confidence_flags = TRUE
)

result <- sus_climate_compute_indicators(
  df_clima,
  region              = "auto",
  verify_physics      = TRUE,
  compute_uncertainty = TRUE,
  keep_source_vars    = TRUE
)

df_clima |>
  sus_climate_fill_inmet(target_var = "all") |>
  sus_climate_compute_indicators(indicators = c("wbgt", "hi", "utci"))
} # }
